tldr: When generating robot manipulation data from human first-person (egocentric) videos, this study converts motions based on "contact points and forces on object surfaces" rather than geometric hand movements. This prevents fingers from hovering and grippers from missing objects, substantially improving VLA model success rates without any simulator demonstrations.
hero_caption: Overview of the Ego2X overall pipeline and the CORE representation. From a monocular video, hands and objects are reconstructed to extract object-centric contact information (CORE). It seamlessly handles depth correction, IK across diverse robot embodiments, video compositing that prevents object degradation, and physical verification in simulation.
overview:
Massive amounts of physical interaction data are essential for training embodied AI and robot foundation models, but collecting teleoperation data on physical robots is labor-intensive and costly. While using first-person videos capturing everyday human tasks has gained significant traction, existing methods suffer from a fatal flaw. Because prior pipelines geometrically mapped 3D hand trajectories to robot joints, monocular depth ambiguity caused fingers to hover beside objects and parallel grippers to close on empty air, failing physically.

To tackle this, the authors returned to an object-centric perspective: "what matters is how the object moves and what contacts drive that motion," proposing a new framework called "Ego2X." At its heart lies CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), a unified representation that records contact positions, grasp modes, estimated contact forces, and interaction states in the object's coordinate frame.

This study introduces a "decoupled depth correction" to prevent mutual hand-object scale ambiguities from amplifying errors in an interdependent loop. It also builds contact-driven inverse kinematics (IK) that automatically interprets contact surfaces from URDFs for dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Experimental results show that the contact realization rate for dexterous hands jumps from 27.9% with prior methods to 62.9%. Furthermore, post-training a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model solely on converted data without any human simulator demonstrations elevated task success rates from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0%.
contributions: Proposed CORE, a contact-centric object-interaction representation that unifies contact points, force distributions, grasp modes, and task phases in the object's local frame.
Built a decoupled depth correction pipeline that fixes line-of-sight depth drift inherent to monocular video down to the millimeter level, avoiding error loops between hand and object scales.
Established a retargeting method supporting both dexterous hands and parallel 2-jaw grippers, automatically allocating contact pads from URDFs to realize physically viable contacts.
Achieved contact boundary preservation and skin-tone separation rendering in video compositing, preventing held objects from being erased when replacing human arms with robot arms.

Demonstrated that post-training a VLA model solely on data converted and physically verified from egocentric videos—without adding any physical robot or simulator demonstrations—significantly boosts manipulation task success rates.

sections.heading: From visual mimicry to physically viable contact transfer
sections.summary: Conventional approaches for generating robot motions from egocentric video mainly mimic 3D hand movements, but monocular depth errors often leave fingers hovering in midair. Ego2X shifts focus from hand motion to surface contacts on objects, converting human demonstrations into physically executable motions for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.
sections.details:
Recently, human first-person (egocentric) videos have drawn widespread attention as training data for robot foundation models such as VLAs. However, previous approaches (e.g., Phantom, EgoMimic, HuRo, Ego2Robot) focus primarily on mapping the 3D trajectories of human hands and arms to robot joints.

A fundamental problem here is that hand positions estimated from monocular RGB cameras suffer from line-of-sight depth drift on the order of centimeters. Successful object manipulation requires millimeter-level precision at the object surface. A drift of several centimeters means fingers hover in empty air or parallel grippers close without grasping anything.

Overcoming this requires solving three key challenges: (1) breaking the circular dependency where hand and object scale estimations corrupt each other, (2) recovering contact timing and force allocation across occluded contact surfaces from monocular images, and (3) retargeting across diverse robot morphologies (dexterous hands and parallel grippers) that have different kinematic link structures and contact pads from human hands.

Ego2X places CORE, a novel representation describing surface events in the object coordinate frame, at its center. It provides a contact-driven pipeline across geometric correction, retargeting, arm erasure, robot compositing, and simulation-based physical verification. This enables the automatic generation of high-quality, physically sound robot demonstrations from monocular egocentric videos.

sections.heading: At the intersection of video imitation, contact estimation, and cross-embodiment retargeting
sections.summary: This section surveys four related fields: learning manipulation from human video, 3D hand-object contact reconstruction, cross-embodiment retargeting, and video compositing, positioning how Ego2X bridges them through the unifying concept of object-frame contact.
sections.details:
The work connects across four major research domains:

- Manipulation Learning from Human Video: Techniques range from aligning latent policy spaces and erasing human hands to redraw robot arms (e.g., Phantom) to directly mapping 3D joint angles (e.g., HuRo, Ego2Robot). However, these focus on free-space hand motion or wrist trajectories and fail to guarantee physical contact dynamics at the object surface.
- Hand-Object Reconstruction and Contact Estimation: Alongside advances in 3D hand mesh estimation from monocular RGB (e.g., EgoHand) and 6D object pose tracking (e.g., FoundationPose), contact detection via visual-tactile cues (e.g., EgoTac) has progressed. Ego2X incorporates these insights into depth correction without coupling hand and object scales.
- Cross-Embodiment Retargeting: Converting human hand motion to dexterous robot hands traditionally required ground-truth object trajectories or training reinforcement learning tracking policies for individual clips. Ego2X parses URDF files, automatically assigns contact pads, and solves contact-driven inverse kinematics (IK) efficiently using optimization.
- Robot Video Compositing and Physical Verification: Video inpainting replaces humans with robots, while simulators verify physical feasibility. Ego2X pairs object-preserving masking and skin removal with closed-loop simulation checks driven by CORE interaction states.

(c) Decoupled depth correction fixes line-of-sight drift, followed by (d) clean video compositing that preserves hand-object boundaries, (e) physical simulation pass/fail filtering, and (f) final dataset export across multiple robot embodiments.

sections.heading: The CORE representation and the contact-driven conversion pipeline
sections.summary: Ego2X reconstructs hands and object SDFs from monocular video, logging contact points, forces, modes, and states as CORE on the object surface. This representation powers decoupled depth correction, contact-driven IK across embodiments, object-preserving video compositing, and simulation verification.
sections.details:
The Ego2X pipeline converts input videos into executable robot episodes through the following steps:

### 3.1 Hand and Object Geometric Reconstruction
First, a gravity-aligned, metric world coordinate frame is established. For hands, WiLoR and ACE-Ego-Hand detect hand regions, EgoHand estimates 3D skeletons, and a MANO hand mesh (partitioned into 24 regions) is fitted per frame. For objects, SAM 3D reconstructs a Signed Distance Field (SDF) $\phi_o$, and FoundationPose performs 6D pose tracking.

### 3.2 Contact-Centric Object-Interaction REpresentation (CORE)
CORE defines a per-frame 4-tuple in the object frame, $\mathbf{c}_{t,k} = (\mathbf{p}_{t,k}, \mathbf{f}_{t,k}, m_{t,k}, s_{t,k})$, with confidence tiers (Certified, Trusted, Hypothesis, Uncertain):
- Contact Point $\mathbf{p}_{t,k}$: While monocular depth drifts, 2D screen positions remain reliable. Visual-tactile detection (EgoTac) identifies contact timing, and rays cast from hand vertices intersect with the object SDF $\phi_o$. These intersections are clustered by medoids to establish surface anchors.
- Grasp Mode $m_{t,k}$ and Interaction State $s_{t,k}$: Seven grasp modes (Table 1: power grasps, pinches, etc.) are determined from contacting hand regions, and task execution is segmented into five states (Approach, Acquire, Hold, Transport, Release).
- Force Prior $\mathbf{f}_{t,k}$: Because absolute forces in Newtons cannot be measured directly from RGB, forces are modeled as a two-part prior combining a visual finger load allocation $\rho_{t,k}$ with the minimum lower-bound force $f^{\mathrm{lb}}_{t,k}$ needed to balance gravity and acceleration.

### 3.3 CORE-Driven Interaction Recovery
- Decoupled Depth Correction (Section 3.3.1): Using the hand to scale the object while using the object to fix hand depth causes circular error propagation. Ego2X uses a gradient-boosted decision tree (GBDT) to gauge object pose confidence, decoupling object trajectory refinement from a 1D hand translation along the camera ray ($\delta \in [-150, +50]$ mm).
- Contact-Driven Inverse Kinematics (Section 3.3.2): For dexterous hands, an optimization using a robust Geman-McClure loss pulls robot finger pads toward CORE anchors and aligns contact normals and push directions. For parallel grippers, antipodal grasp candidates on the object SDF are evaluated, with opening/closing and rigid attachment scheduled according to interaction states $s_{t,k}$.
- Contact-Aware Erasure and Video Compositing (Section 3.3.3): To prevent held objects from disappearing during arm removal, object preservation masks based on CORE states protect the object from inpainting. Furthermore, a "de-skinning" step in Lab color space removes pixels close to human skin prototypes, preventing skin tones from bleeding onto object edges.

### 3.4 URDF Compilation and Simulation Verification
To support arbitrary robots without manual tuning, a URDF compiler parses collision meshes into a pool of candidate contact pads. Finally, closed-loop physical execution in RoboTwin 2.0 validates trajectories; only episodes that complete tasks without dropping objects receive a passing mark and enter the VLA training dataset.

sections.heading: Sharp gains in contact accuracy and successful VLA post-training without simulator demos
sections.summary: Evaluations across HOT3D, EgoDex, and RoboTwin 2.0 show that Ego2X reduces hand depth error by 33.7%, more than doubles dexterous contact realization over prior methods, and boosts VLA post-training success rates from 40.5% to 67.0% using converted data alone.
sections.details:
Experiments evaluated geometric accuracy, physical contact fidelity, video compositing quality, and downstream VLA policy performance.

### 4.1–4.2 Contact Reconstruction Accuracy
On HOT3D (with ground-truth motion capture meshes), combining visual-tactile cues with ray-casting reduced 3D contact point errors from 6.69 mm (geometric nearest neighbor) to 1.96 mm. Interaction state recognition accuracy also increased from 0.701 to 0.841.

### 4.3 Impact of Decoupled Depth Correction
Decoupling hand and object correction paths reduced hand joint errors (MPJPE) on HOT3D. With HaWoR, in-contact hand depth error along the camera ray dropped from 14.35 mm to 9.51 mm (a 33.7% reduction). Median object translation error improved from 104.6 mm to 67.3 mm, validating the decoupled design.

### 4.4 Contact Retargeting Across Embodiments
On EgoDex (79 takes), the contact realization rate for dexterous hands reached 62.9% (89.5% in high-confidence regions) with the proposed method (CARD), outperforming wrist-following baselines and the official HuRo pipeline (27.9%–29.6%). For parallel grippers, physical contact realization reached 63.2%, compared to 9.7% for Ego2Robot.

### 4.5 Quality of Contact-Aware Video Compositing
Object clipping caused by inpainting dropped from 19.4%–55.0% under naive masking to 3.0%–11.2% with contact-aware protection. Lab color space de-skinning eliminated skin-tone bleeding at hand-object boundaries from 12.55% down to 0.00%.

### 4.6 Closed-Loop Verification and VLA Policy Post-Training
In RoboTwin 2.0 closed-loop simulation checks, prior pipelines (HuRo and Ego2Robot) achieved only a 1.9% pass rate (1/52 episodes) on a bread-in-basket task, whereas Ego2X achieved 59.6% (31/52 episodes).

Most notably, when post-training an X-VLA policy exclusively on Ego2X episodes—without any simulator demonstrations—task success across 200 unseen paired scenes rose from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0%. This approaches the 72.0% success rate achieved when using 20 in-domain simulator demonstrations. In contrast, training on raw, unverified converted data achieved only 41.0%–44.5%, hovering close to zero-shot performance.

(b) Contact error ablation on HOT3D shows errors drop to 1.96 mm when combining visual-tactile detection with ray casting (T+R). (c) Substantial improvements in state recognition across 31 evaluation clips.

sections.heading: Conclusions and outlook: building a scalable, cross-embodiment data foundation
sections.summary: Ego2X establishes a framework for converting first-person videos into physically executable robot manipulation data via CORE. Improving VLA performance by 26.5 percentage points without simulator demonstrations opens a scalable pathway for post-training foundation models.
sections.details:
This work presented Ego2X to translate human egocentric videos into executable demonstrations across various robots. Shifting from geometric wrist-tracking to transferring contacts directly on object surfaces represents its central breakthrough.

Integrating CORE-driven depth correction, contact-aware IK, URDF compilation, object-preserving video rendering, and closed-loop physical verification yields a practical pipeline for scaling robot datasets from human video.

### Limitations and Future Work
The authors highlight three directions for future work:
- Object Pose Tracking Under Heavy Occlusion: When objects are heavily blocked by hands or environments, 6D pose drift degrades surface anchor localization.
- True Contact Forces in Newtons: Because forces currently rely on visual-kinematic priors, integrating physical tactile sensors in future work remains desirable.
- Physical Robot Deployments: Constrained by hardware and timeline considerations, full-scale hardware evaluations were ongoing at publication time, leaving real-world deployment for subsequent studies.

takeaways: When transferring manipulation data to robots, retargeting contact points, force allocations, and grasp modes on object surfaces matters far more than matching 3D hand positions.
Fixing monocular line-of-sight depth drift requires decoupling hand and object scale corrections to prevent circular error propagation.
Replacing human arms with robot embodiments demands contact-aware pixel protection and color de-skinning to avoid clipping held objects or leaking skin artifacts into visual policies.
Filtering converted demonstration data through closed-loop physical simulation enables substantial VLA performance gains without requiring hand-collected simulator demonstrations.
limitations: Severe object occlusion by human hands can degrade upstream 6D object pose tracking, leading to misaligned contact anchors.
Estimated contact forces are visual-kinematic priors rather than exact, sensor-measured forces in Newtons suitable for direct force-control loops.
While extensively evaluated in the RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, end-to-end evaluations on physical hardware robots remain ongoing.
